fields.Q1:
WHAT IS STANDING AROUND THIS ROOM MADE OF?**
I cannot tell. At the size shown there is nothing there to put a hand on. Where the room ends, the image is black — not dark stone, black. I can name a material only after brightening the file by a factor of roughly four, and then it is *flat rectangular blocks with dark joints*, the same blocks as everything else in the frame.
fields.Q1_WHY: I sampled the boundary directly. At y=440 — the figure's own row, the brightest band in the picture — crossing the west edge left to right, x=48→64 reads RGB(6,6,8)(6,6,8)(6,6,8)(6,6,8)(6,6,8)(7,7,9)(7,7,9) | (3,3,4)(3,3,4)(4,4,5)(4,4,5)(4,4,6)(4,4,6)(5,5,6)(5,5,6). A step of **4/255**. The lit floor 200px away averages 114/255. Across the north band (y=174–202, x=55–690), **87.4% of pixels are below 20/255** and the single brightest pixel anywhere in that band is 38. There is no material information in the file at that level.
fields.Q2:
SOLID MASS, OR A FLAT PATTERN AROUND THE EDGE?**
**Flat pattern.** Not a judgement call — magnified, the north edge is literally three continuous horizontal rules with ticks between them. At y=173, y=187 and y=203 there are near-unbroken dark lines: y=187 is darker than the row two pixels above it for 70% of the 635px span, y=203 for 83%. Between them sit two courses of rectangles of **identical height, unstaggered, running the full width with no bond and no break**. It is a ladder diagram of a wall.

Three further things confirm it has no thickness:
- **No contact shadow.** Down column x=300 the values from y=200 to y=230 run 10.3, 10.3, 17.3, 22.7, 28.3, 34.7, 44.3 — a smooth lighting ramp. Nothing is casting anything onto the floor.
- **No corner.** At the NW corner the north band simply stops at x=54 and does not turn. There is no return piece.
- **The joint weight in the wall and the joint weight in the floor two pixels below it are the same line.**
fields.Q3:
WHERE EXACTLY DOES THE GROUND STOP?**
Three edges, all **one pixel**:
- **North, y=170.** Strongest horizontal seam in the frame (0.145 mean adjacent-row delta). Then the 30px two-course band to y=203.
- **West, x=54.** Strongest vertical seam (0.073, twice any other column). One pixel. West of it is a flat field of wide horizontal stripes with no grain, no joints, no cracks. East of it is textured floor.
- **South, y=714.** One dark pixel row, then a flat field of soft vertical stripes.
- **East: there is no edge at all.** I scanned every column: the strongest candidate near x=688 measures 0.035, which is indistinguishable from an ordinary interior grout line. The tile grid runs unbroken from x=650 to the frame edge at x=750. The right side of the room appears to end only because the torch stops reaching. **This room has no east wall and no west wall — it has a change of wallpaper on one side and nothing on the other.**
fields.Q4:
WHAT IS HOLDING THIS PLACE TOGETHER?**
**NOTHING.** I looked for it specifically. There is not one pin, rope, brace, strap, plate, timber, wedge or driven fixing anywhere on a standing surface. The only made object in the entire frame is a ladder at x=128–147, y=130–168 — a post with three rungs — and it is *outside* the room, north of the wall line, at luminance ~10/255, i.e. invisible unless you brighten the file. For a place held by a company that has been repairing it with rope and driven pins for four hundred years, there is no evidence of hands on this structure at all.
fields.Q5:
BUILT, OR AN IMAGE THAT WAS REPEATED?**
**Repeated.** Not tiled — I ran high-pass autocorrelation over the lit interior and found no periodic peak at any offset from 4 to 90px, so the generator is varying its rectangles. But *varying a rectangle is not building*. The same grammar — axis-aligned block, 1px dark joint — produces the floor, the wall, the corridor, the ground beyond the west seam and the ground beyond the south seam, at the same line weight, with no rule ever changing to say "this one stands up." A builder makes a wall differently from a floor. This made them the same and then dimmed one.
fields.Q6:
WOULD YOU BELIEVE THIS SHIPPED IN A COMMERCIAL GAME?**
**NO.** On the second question it does not arise — but to answer it straight: it is not merely competent either. A shipped tile set has a wall you can see. This one is 87% below 20/255.
fields.Q7:
WHAT CAN YOU ACTUALLY SEE ON THE STANDING SURFACES AT 1:1?**
Nothing. Every standing surface in this frame is blank at 1:1 — not sparse, not subtle, blank. The one exception: a faint vertical lightening at top-centre, and that is torchlight spill, not surface.

Everything below required magnification and a gamma boost: two brick courses in the north band; the unstaggered middle rule; the corridor jambs at x=377 and x=440; the ladder at (128–147, 130–168); the second wall band lying west of the seam at y=427–460; the flat-panel object at (180–248, 395–460).

It does **not** change with distance from the figure in the way it should. The wall's best pixel is 38/255 at x=380 — directly in the light, 200px from the torch. At x=100, still well inside the lit radius, the band means 3.9. The lighting is not revealing the wall anywhere, at any distance. There is nothing there for it to reveal.
fields.Q8:
ANYTHING YOUR EYE KEEPS RETURNING TO?**
Yes, three things, all in the north band y=173–203:

1. **The middle rule at y=187 never breaks.** It runs 635 pixels straight through, and the two courses never offset. There is no bond. Every real wall in the world staggers, and this one has been holding for four hundred years without doing so.
2. **Every vertical tick between blocks is exactly 1px wide, everywhere.** Not one is wider, doubled, chipped or filled.
3. **The rule at y=203 that ends the wall and the grout lines at y=205, 220, 235 that divide the floor are the same weight.** Once I saw that, I could not stop seeing it: nothing in the drawing distinguishes the edge of a standing thing from a line scratched on the ground.
fields.Q9:
WHAT IS BEYOND THE WALLS?**
More ground. Not mass, not void, not a room I can't see into — more floor, differently patterned. West of x=54 is a flat field of wide horizontal stripes; south of y=714 is a field of soft vertical stripes; north of y=170 is a field of larger flat blocks, with a ladder standing on it. All of it sits at the same apparent height as the room I'm in, with no lip, no shadow, no occlusion. I am not looking at the far side of a wall. I am looking at the next floor tile along, in a different colour.

At 1:1 none of this is visible; beyond the walls is black. That black reads as *empty screen*, not as unlit stone — because nothing in the near-black is textured enough to suggest anything is there.
fields.Q10:
COULD YOU TELL A WAY THROUGH FROM A DEAD END WITHOUT WALKING INTO IT?**
I found it: a channel from x≈377 to x≈440, running north from the room mouth at y≈203 to the top of the frame. At 1:1 I can see it — a faint lighter vertical strip above the room.

But I read it as **a smear of light, not a passage.** What makes it visible is that the torch spills up it: inside the channel luminance is 12–16, the band either side is ~5. What makes a passage *readable* is its jambs, and the jambs here are at 5/255 — invisible. The corridor is only legible because it happens to lie north of the figure, in the direction the light gradient reaches. Put the same corridor on the west edge and I would have walked into it. **So the honest answer to the question as asked is no** — I can tell there is light going somewhere, which is not the same as being able to read the structure. And that is a navigation problem, not an aesthetic one.
fields.Q11:
HAS ANYTHING HAPPENED TO THIS STRUCTURE?**
Nothing has happened to it. It is unmarked. Magnified, both courses of the north band are clean, square, unchipped and evenly spaced end to end; no block is displaced, cracked, missing, patched or replaced. The thin dark meandering lines in the frame all lie on the ground and stop at the wall line. I read that from the joints: every one is the same width and the same value, and the two courses hold a perfect line for 635 pixels. This is a structure with no history — which is the one thing a place in continuous heavy use since before records began, and never once cared for, cannot be.

---
fields.CULL: The wall is 87% below 20/255 and one pixel thick — at 1:1 there is no wall.
fields.FLIP LIST:
- Give the wall a lit face: raise the standing band to a floor-relative value that stays legible at 1:1 in the dark zone, and hold it at a fixed offset from the floor so it never falls below readability regardless of torch distance.
- Give it thickness: a top face plus a distinct near-side face, and a contact shadow cast onto the floor at y≈203 — currently the ramp from y=200 to y=230 is 10, 10, 17, 23, 28, 35, 44 with nothing dark in it.
- Draw the east and west edges. There is no east wall at all (strongest column candidate 0.035, same as an interior grout line) and the west edge at x=54 is a 4/255 change of pattern. The room must be bounded on all four sides by the same drawn object.
- Break the two-course band: stagger the bond, vary course heights, and stop the y=187 rule running 635px unbroken. Make the wall joint weight visibly heavier than the floor joint weight.
- Put the orcs' work on it: driven pins, lashed rope, a hide patch, a salvaged timber brace — at a scale readable at 1:1 — and at least one displaced or replaced block, so the wall carries four hundred years of repair instead of none.

---
*Model: Claude Opus 5 (1M context)*
